Headline: Citizens Bank Partners with NCHL to Launch NEPALPAY Card Services
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited has signed an agreement with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to enable payment processing of NEPALPAY Cards through NCHL’s EFT Card Switch. With this collaboration, Citizens Bank becomes the first EFT member bank officially onboarded to acquire and issue NEPALPAY Cards.
Under the first phase, the bank will allow NEPALPAY Card transactions across its 168 ATMs and 491 POS terminals, and later issue the cards to its customers.
The NEPALPAY Card, launched as Nepal’s national card scheme under the National Payment Switch (NPS), allows domestic transactions and international acceptance through its partnership with the Discover® Network.
More than 34 banks and financial institutions have subscribed to NEPALPAY, with several preparing for rollout. Serving over 1.8 million customers, Citizens Bank continues to strengthen its digital transformation efforts through its wide network of branches, ATMs, and banking channels.

Headline: Falgun Interest Rate Update: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates; Majority Keep Rates Unchanged
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Falgun, showing a decline compared to Poush.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 8 have reduced their rates, while the remaining 12 banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Global IME Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on individual fixed deposits by 0.75 percentage points.
Meanwhile Citizens Bank International , Himalayan Bank, kumari Bank, Laxmi Sunrise Bank, Maccha puchre Bank, Nabil Bank, Nepal Bank, NIC Asia Bank, NMB Bank, Prabhu Bank, Rastriya Banjiya Bank and Sanima Bank have maintained the same rates as in Poush.

Headline: Citizens Bank and NCHL Sign Agreement to Issue NepalPay Card
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) and Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) have signed an agreement under the National Payment Switch (NPS) to operate the NepalPay Card through the EFT switch. With this partnership, Citizens Bank becomes the first EFT member bank to issue the domestic NepalPay Card. The bank’s ATMs and POS terminals will also accept international cards such as Discover, Diners, and Pulse. Customers will soon receive Nepal’s own card scheme, NepalPay Card.
The bank has also introduced several digital innovations, including a virtual credit card in collaboration with Fonepay, Gen-Z–focused savings accounts, a unified “Digi Bank” platform, freelancer-targeted accounts, and mobile banking services for share applications and CRN numbers. Currently, the bank serves nearly 2 million customers through 200 branches, 169 ATMs, and multiple service units across 61 districts of Nepal.

Headline: Citizens Bank Honors Gaurab Uprety with MAN–Citizens Aspiring Manager Award
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited has awarded Gaurab Uprety with the “MAN–Citizens Aspiring Manager Award” at the National Management Convention organized by the Management Association of Nepal (MAN) on Magh 24, 2082. The award, presented by Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut, aims to promote excellence in management education. Established through an agreement between Citizens Bank and MAN, the award carries Rs 51,000 and is given annually to the top-performing MBA student of Purbanchal University.
The bank, a recipient of the Bank of the Year 2024 and 2025 titles, continues to expand innovative services, including Nepal’s first Citizens Fonepay Virtual Credit Card, Gen-Z Savings Account, Digi Bank online platform, Freelancer Savings Account, and mobile banking–based share application and CRN services, along with cross-bank teller QR cash withdrawal. Citizens Bank currently serves over 1.97 million customers through its nationwide network of 200 branches, 169 ATMs, and multiple service outlets across 61 districts.

Headline: Citizens Bank Organizes Cancer Awareness Programs for Employees
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) organized breast and prostate cancer awareness programs to promote health consciousness among its employees. Conducted in collaboration with Medanta - The Medicity Hospital, Gurugram, India, the initiative focused on providing accurate information, addressing common myths, and highlighting the importance of early detection, prevention, and timely medical consultation.
Separate webinars were held for female and male employees, drawing strong participation and interactive engagement. The bank stated that the program aims to contribute to long-term health security and reaffirmed its commitment to organizing similar awareness initiatives in the future. Additionally, CZBIL has extended up to a 15 percent discount on treatment services at Medanta Hospital for its card-holding customers, reinforcing its focus on employee and customer well-being.

Headline: Citizens Bank International Reports a 45.78% Decline in Net Profit in Q2; Distributable Profit Is In Negative
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL)
has unveiled its second-quarter report for 2082/83, reflecting a 45.78% decline in Net profit.  As per the report, the net profit decreased to Rs. 35.88 crore as compared to Rs 66.18 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The decline in profitability was largely due to higher impairment charges and a decline in operating profit.
The bank has a total paid-up capital of Rs. 15.5 Arba and reserves amounting to Rs. 8.82 Arba. However, the retained earnings stood at a negative Rs 1.1 Arba. Operating profit for the period declined by 44.68% to Rs. 50.41 crores, while impairment charges surged by 32.30% to Rs. 1.83 arba.
During this quarter, the bank's total deposits slightly declined by 0.60%  to Rs 2.10 Kharba, with loans and advances to customers reaching Rs 1.68 Kharba. The bank’s net interest income stood at Rs. 3.14 arba, up by 2.28% from Rs. 3.07 arba last year.
Examining financial metrics, the second quarter reported an annualised EPS of Rs 4.63, and the net worth per share stood at Rs 149.79. The capital adequacy ratio decreased to 12.43% from 12.87%. Additionally, the disclosure of a negative distributable profit of Rs. 1.10 Arba adds a notable dimension to CZBIL's financial narrative during this period.

Headline: Citizens Santulit Yojana Oversubscribed by Over 25%
Full Content:
Citizens Capital Limited’s fourth close-ended mutual fund scheme, Citizens Santulit Yojana, has received overwhelming investor response, with applications exceeding the targeted fund size of Rs. 1 Arba by more than 25 percent.
Approved by the Securities Board of Nepal, the public issue was open from Poush 4 to Poush 18, during which both individual and institutional investors submitted applications worth over Rs. 1 Arba 25 Crores.
The strong participation reflects growing investor confidence in Citizens Capital as a professional and reliable institution in Nepal’s capital market.
Citizens Capital, a subsidiary of Citizens Bank International, provides a wide range of financial services and has reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, good governance, and delivering competitive returns to investors.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Kartik; GBIME Tops the Charts
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the fourth month of the fiscal year 2082/83, ending in Kartik.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 19.37 Arba. Global IME Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 2.51 Arba, overtaking Nabil Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 2.46 Crores. Prime Commercial Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 1.58 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and NMB Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Citizens Bank International recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 1.64 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 1.79 Arba, despite eight out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Garima Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 39.77 Crores, outpacing Garima Bikas Bank, Muktinath Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 38.42 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 30.25 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Miteri Development Bank and Green Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 3.5 Crores and Rs. 2.18 Crores, respectively.
Furthermore, seven banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, Salapa, Lumbini Bikas Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Citizens Bank Wins Prestigious Bank of the Year 2025 Award
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL), serving Nepal for the past 19 years, has been awarded the prestigious Bank of the Year 2025 by The Financial Times in London. Chairman Prabal Jung Pandey and CEO Ganesh Raj Pokharel received the award on behalf of the bank. This is the bank’s second consecutive win, having also secured the Bank of the Year 2024 title.
The ceremony saw participation from over 400 banking leaders representing more than 125 countries. The bank’s leadership expressed pride in earning what is considered the “Oscars of Banking,” noting that the recognition motivates them to further strengthen modern, customer-friendly, transparent, and sustainable banking services.
Citizens Bank has recently introduced several innovations, including Nepal’s first Citizens FonePay Virtual Credit Card, the Gen-Z savings account, the integrated Citizens DigiBank platform, and a special Freelancer Savings Account.
The bank also offers unique services like share application and CRN generation via mobile banking and cross-bank teller cash withdrawal through QR scan. With a widespread network of 200 branches, 169 ATMs, and 42 branchless units across 61 districts, Citizens Bank continues to serve nearly 2 million customers nationwide.

Headline: Citizens Bank Approves 5% Bonus Share and Expands Digital Innovations at 19th AGM
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited held its 19th Annual General Meeting (AGM) under the chairmanship of Prabal Jung Pandey in Kathmandu. The AGM approved the Board’s annual report, auditor’s report, and consolidated financial statements for FY 2081/82. Shareholders unanimously passed the proposal to distribute a 5% bonus share (Rs. 738.45 million) and 0.263% cash dividend for tax purposes, totaling Rs. 777.31 million. The bank has consistently distributed dividends since FY 065/66, with an average of 10.40% over 19 years.
The chairman assured shareholders that the bank is committed to strong governance, compliance, and future growth. Citizens Bank recently won the prestigious “Bank of the Year 2024” award and has introduced several innovative services, including Nepal’s first Citizens FonePay Virtual Credit Card, youth-focused savings accounts, integrated digital banking, freelancer accounts, share application through mobile banking, CRN services, and cross-bank teller QR cash withdrawal. The bank currently serves 1.956 million customers through 200 branches, 169 ATMs, 3 extension counters, and 42 branchless units across 61 districts.

Headline: Citizens Bank Launches “Gen-Z Saving Account” Targeting Youth and Digital Users
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited has introduced a new youth-focused savings product called the “Citizens Gen-Z Saving Account.” The account was officially launched on 8 Mangsir 2082 by CEO Ganesh Raj Pokharel. Designed for students, freelancers, creators, entrepreneurs, and digitally active youth, the account aims to provide financial solutions aligned with modern lifestyles.
The account can be opened with just Rs. 100 and offers a 3.02% annual interest rate. Customers receive several free services in the first year, including a cheque book, DEMAT account, C-ASBA commission, and C-ASBA registration. A bundled digital package, ATM card, mobile banking, e-comm card, and internet banking, is available for only Rs. 500. Users also get 50% off on travel card issuance, a customized Gen-Z dashboard on mobile banking, and 25% cashback on their first mobile top-up.
Citizens Bank, recently awarded “Bank of the Year 2024,” continues to innovate with products like Nepal’s first virtual credit card with Fonepay and a dedicated Freelancer Savings Account. The bank provides services through 200 branches, 169 ATMs, 3 extension counters, and 42 branchless units across 61 districts, serving over 1.95 million customers.

Headline: Unveiling Q1 FY 2082/83: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the first quarter of FY 2082/83, offering a fresh look into their performance during the third-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q1 FY 2082/83, Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led with a net profit of Rs. 1.86 Arba, marking a 22.88% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 1.76 Arba, though this represents a 14.59 % decrease from the previous year. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 1.26 Arba.
Ratriya Banjiya Bank Limited (RBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 295.24% rise, while Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) saw the largest decline at 211.11%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.75 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 18.78 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 38.38 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 38.07 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 32.73 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 66.02 Kharba in customer deposits, with nine banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.82 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.56 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 5.28 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.29 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.21 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) also with Rs. 4.21 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 70.12 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 7.01 Kharba, with six banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 4.13 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 3.90 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 20.13 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 2.80 Arba, with Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) next at lowest Rs. 0.18 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Annualized Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 36.44, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at Rs. 27.57 and Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at Rs.26.53. The industry average EPS was Rs.13.80, with ten banks above this benchmark. Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 5.97.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 42.46 per share, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at Rs. 24.01. Seven banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs 339.91, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs 278.73 and Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs 260.32. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs 145.21, while the industry average stood at Rs 203.84.
*Note: Preference Share is excluded while calculating the Net worth of Agriculture Development Bank (ADBL).
P/E Ratio:
Prime Commercial Limited (PCBL) had the lowest P/E ratio at 8.97 times, followed by Kumari Bank Limited (kBL) at 11.26 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 18.60%, while NMB Bank Limited (NMB) reported the lowest at 12.07%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.74%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.39%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) recorded the highest ROE at 14.47% and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest ROA at 1.71%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 6.36%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 2.89%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 82.65%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 62.39%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 6.60%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the lowest at 4.27%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.2% to 3.9%.

Headline: Citizens Bank Partners with Ekta Books to Offer Special Discounts to Customers

Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) has signed an agreement with Ekta Books, Thapathali, Kathmandu, to provide special benefits to its customers. Under this agreement, cardholders and mobile banking users of Citizens Bank can enjoy up to a 15% discount at Ekta Books outlets in Thapathali, Manbhawan, Pokhara, and Itahari. Headline: Citizens Bank Launches “QR Merchant Loan” for SMEs with Fully Digital Access
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) has introduced the “QR Merchant Loan”, a fully digital lending facility for small and medium-sized businesses affiliated with the bank’s QR merchant system. Eligible businesses, registered for at least 6 months, can apply online or via mobile and receive loans up to 25% of their average monthly QR transaction, ranging from NPR 50,000 to NPR 5,00,000, repayable in monthly installments.
The initiative aims to enhance financial accessibility and support business growth for SMEs. This launch complements Citizens Bank’s ongoing innovations, including virtual credit cards with Fonepay, freelancer-focused savings accounts, and mobile banking services for share applications, serving over 1.94 million customers across 200 branches and 169 ATMs in 61 districts.

Headline: Dividend Spotlight: A Closer Look into Dividend Declarations by Companies Across All Sectors for FY 2081/82
Full Content:
A number of companies listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) have declared dividends for their shareholders for fiscal year 2081/82, reflecting their financial performance and commitment to investor returns. The announcements cover a broad range of sectors, with dividend distributions seen across Banking, Development Bank, Finance, Hotels and Tourism, Hydropower, Investment, Manufacturing and Processing, Microfinance, and Mutual Fund categories. These declarations include both cash and bonus shares, highlighting the varying strategies companies have adopted to reward their investors.
Meanwhile, four sectors, Life Insurance, Non-Life Insurance, Others, and Trading, have not declared any dividends this year. This contrast underscores the differing profitability levels and market conditions across industries within NEPSE. The overall dividend landscape offers valuable insights into the strength and stability of Nepal’s listed companies, serving as a key indicator for investor confidence and sectoral performance in the current fiscal period.
The following data presents a detailed breakdown of all the companies from each sector that have declared dividends this fiscal year:
Commercial Banks
The table below presents the list of commercial banks listed under the Banking Index that have declared dividends this fiscal year, along with details on bonus shares, cash dividends, AGM dates, and book closure dates.
Out of the 19 commercial banks listed under the Banking Index, only seven have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Everest Bank (EBL) declared the highest total dividend among commercial banks, distributing 20% in total, comprising 6% bonus shares and a 14% cash dividend.
Development Banks
Out of the 16 development banks listed under the Development Bank Index, only four have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) distributed the highest total dividend of 18.20%, including 13.53% bonus shares and a 4.67% cash dividend.
In contrast, Miteri Development Bank (MDB) declared the lowest dividend among development banks, offering only a 10% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Finance
Only one finance company, Manjushree Finance (MFIL), has declared a dividend for FY 2081/82. The company announced a 15% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Hotels and Tourism
From the Hotel and Tourism sector, only Soaltee Hotel (SHL) announced the total dividend of 31.5789%, comprising 15% bonus shares and a 16.5789% cash dividend.
Hydropower
Among the 94 hydropower companies listed under the Hydropower Index, only five have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Bhagawati Hydropower Development Company (BGWT) distributed the highest total dividend of 20%, comprising 14% bonus shares and a 6% cash dividend.
At the lower end, Arun Valley Hydropower Development Company (AHPC) announced a total dividend of 8.421%, including 8% bonus shares and a 0.421% cash dividend. The overall declarations from the sector suggest selective profitability, with only a handful of hydropower companies managing to reward shareholders this fiscal year.
Investment
Out of seven companies in the sector, only Hathway Investment Nepal (HATHY) and Nepal Infrastructure Bank (NIFRA) have announced dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Hathway Investment has declared a total dividend of 12.632%, including a 12% bonus share and 0.632% cash dividend. The company’s AGM was scheduled for Bhadra 25, 2082, with the book closure date on Bhadra 13, 2082.
Nepal Infrastructure Bank has declared a 6.3158% cash dividend, without issuing bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for NIFRA have not yet been announced.
Manufacturing and Processing
In the Manufacturing sector, only Himalayan Distillery (HDL), Nepal Lube Oil (NLO), and Unilever Nepal (UNL) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Himalayan Distillery has announced a total dividend of 25%, including a 20% bonus share and 5% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 30, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 20, 2082.
Nepal Lube Oil declared a total dividend of 21.05264%, comprising a 20% bonus share and 1.05264% cash dividend. The AGM was set for Ashwin 31, 2082, with the book closure date on Ashwin 12, 2082.
Unilever Nepal announced a cash dividend of 1842%, with no bonus shares. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 25, 2082, and the book closure period is Kartik 11–25, 2082.
Microfinance
In the Microfinance sector, only Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (GLBSL) and RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (RSDC) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha has announced a total dividend of 15%, consisting of a 14.25% bonus share and 0.75% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 23, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 14, 2082.
RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha declared an 8% cash dividend, with no bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for RSDC have not yet been announced.
Mutual Fund
All 52 mutual funds have declared cash dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82. Notable funds include Laxmi Unnati Kosh (20%), Sanima Large Cap Fund (21.05%), Siddhartha Equity Fund (20%), RBB Mutual Fund 1 (20%), and Sunrise Bluechip Fund (19%). Other funds have announced dividends between 5% and 20%.

Full Content:

Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL).

Headline: Citizens Bank Partners with Kathmandu Medical College to Offer Discounts on Specialist Services
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) has signed an agreement with Kathmandu Medical College, Sinamangal, to provide its cardholders and mobile banking customers with up to 15% discount on specialist medical services. The collaboration aims to promote digital transactions over cash payments.
The bank, which recently won the “Bank of the Year 2024” award, continues to introduce innovative digital services, including Nepal’s first “Citizens Fonepay Credit Card”, a Freelancer Service Account, and CRN and share application features via mobile banking. With 200 branches, 169 ATMs, and 19.44 lakh customers across 61 districts, Citizens Bank remains committed to expanding convenient, customer-friendly digital banking facilities nationwide.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Kartik Interest Rates; Machhapuchchhre Bank and NMB Bank Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Kartik, showing a decline compared to Ashwin.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 14 have reduced their rates, while six banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Machhapuchchhre Bank and NMB Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on both individual and institutional fixed deposits by 1 percentage point. Meanwhile, Nepal Bank, Siddhartha Bank, Rastriya Banijya Bank, Kumari Bank, Global IME Bank, and Himalayan Bank have maintained the same rates as in Ashwin.

Headline: Citizens Bank International Limited Proposes 5.263% Dividend for FY 2081/82
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL)
has proposed a 5.263% dividend for the fiscal year 2081/82.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Shrawan; GBIME Tops the Charts
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the first month of the fiscal year 2082/83, ending in Shrawan.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 8.38 Arba. Global IME Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 78.45 Crores, overtaking Nabil Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 71.64 Crores. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 63.42 Crores for the period.
Other notable performers include Rastriya Banijya Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Agricultural Development Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 37.50 lakhs.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 81.64 Crores, despite five out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 15.72 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 13.39 Crores in net profit. Lumbini Bikas Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 11.08 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Saptakoshi Development Bank and Salapa Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 32.4 lakhs and Rs. 6.9 lakhs, respectively.
Furthermore, five banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Interest Rates for Ashwin; Nine Banks Slash, Two Raise
Full Content:
Commercial banks have released their revised interest rates for the month of Ashwin, showing a slight overall decline compared to Bhadra. Out of the 20 commercial banks, nine banks maintained their rates unchanged, while 11 banks introduced adjustments. Among these, nine banks lowered their rates, whereas two banks opted for an increase.
Prime Commercial Bank, Sanima Bank, and Everest Bank have each reduced the maximum interest rate on personal term deposits by 0.5 percentage points compared to Bhadra. Citizens Bank and NIC Asia Bank followed with reductions of 0.25 percentage points, while Kumari Bank trimmed its rate by 0.2 percentage points.
Conversely, two banks raised their deposit rates for Ashwin. Laxmi Sunrise Bank increased its maximum personal term deposit rate by 0.25 percentage points, and Standard Chartered Bank made a smaller upward adjustment of 0.05 percentage points.

Headline: Citizens Bank Hosts Leadership Seminar and Reports Strong Double-Digit Growth Across Key Financial Indicators
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited recently organized the “Inspiring Leadership and Performance Seminar on Achieved Budget Goals and Operational Success in Gandaki, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim” for provincial heads, cluster heads, branch managers, and staff. The seminar, attended by CEO Ganesh Raj Pokharel and senior executives, reviewed last fiscal year’s performance, discussed priorities for the current year, and emphasized strengthening collaboration between central and provincial offices.
The bank reported double-digit growth in key indicators for FY 2081/82, including an 11.15% increase in loan disbursement (reaching NPR 1.75 trillion), an 11.69% rise in deposits (totaling NPR 2.14 trillion), and an 11.20% growth in net interest income (NPR 636 million). The bank maintained a CD ratio of 81.91%, ROA of 0.55%, and ROE of 5.81%.
Citizens Bank has also pioneered digital banking innovations in Nepal, launching the Citizens PhonePe Credit Card and enabling share applications and CRN services through its mobile app. With 200 branches, 169 ATMs, 3 extended counters, and 74 branchless banking units across 61 districts, the bank serves over 1.93 million customers with modern banking services.

Full Content:

Headline: CZBIL Holds Koshi Leadership Seminar Amid Strong Growth and Innovative Banking Initiatives
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) organized the “Seminar on Koshi Leadership: Inspiring Performance and Achieving Excellence” for its provincial heads, cluster heads, branch managers, and staff in Koshi Province, with the participation of CEO Ganeshraj Pokharel and senior executives. The seminar reviewed last fiscal year’s performance and discussed priorities for the current year, aiming to strengthen coordination between the central and provincial offices. Similar seminars were recently held in Madhesh and Bagmati provinces, and CZBIL plans to conduct them across other provinces.
In FY 2081/82, the bank achieved double-digit growth in key indicators: loans increased by 11.15% to NPR 1.75 trillion, deposits grew 11.69% to NPR 2.14 trillion, and net interest income rose 11.20% to NPR 636 million. The bank maintained a balanced liquidity with a credit-deposit ratio of 81.91%, ROA of 0.55%, and ROE of 5.81%. CZBIL has introduced innovative services, including the first Citizens PhonePe virtual credit card in Nepal and mobile banking-based share application and CRN services. Operating 200 branches, 169 ATMs, 3 extended counters, and 74 branchless banking units across 61 districts, the bank serves over 1.93 million customers with modern banking solutions.

Headline: Bhadra Interest Rate Update: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates; Majority Keep Rates Unchanged
Full Content:
Commercial banks have announced their revised fixed deposit (FD) interest rates for the month of Bhadra. Out of the 20 commercial banks, 11 left their rates unchanged from Shrawan, while nine made adjustments. Among them, eight banks lowered their rates, whereas one opted for an increase.
Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) implemented the sharpest reduction in institutional FD rates, trimming them by 1.13 percentage points—from 6.26% in Shrawan to 5.13% in Bhadra. Similarly, Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) cut its institutional FD rate by 0.75 percentage points, bringing it down to 4% from 4.75% in the previous month.
On the other hand, Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) stood out as the only bank to increase rates, raising its institutional FD rate by 1.10 percentage points—from 4.25% in Shrawan to 5.35% in Bhadra.
In terms of prevailing rates, Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) offers the lowest individual FD rate at 5%, while Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) provides the lowest institutional FD rate at 2.75%. At the higher end, NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) leads with the highest rates, offering 6.25% for individual FDs and 5.25% for institutional FDs.

Headline: Unveiling Q4 2081/82: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the fourth quarter of FY 2081/82, offering a fresh look into their performance during the twelve-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q4 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 7.13 Arba, marking a 15.01% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 6.76 Arba, though this represents a 64.46% increase from the previous year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 6.20 Arba.
Kumari Bank Limited (NBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 45280.14% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 77.03%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.69 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 18.46 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 37.78 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 36.68 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 33.23 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 64.43 Kharba in customer deposits, with eight banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.50 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.24 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 5 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.25 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.13 Kharba, followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) with Rs. 4.12 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 72.21 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.33 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 16.71 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 16.33 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 25.52 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 4.31 Arba, with NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) next at Rs. 4.14 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 37.99, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 27.63 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 26.34. The industry average EPS was Rs. 18.44, with ten banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 1.08.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 38.27 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.47. Four banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 341.59, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 259.81 and Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 243.40. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 142.19, while the industry average stood at Rs. 201.57.
*Note: Preference Share is excluded while calculating the Net worth of Agriculture Development Bank (ADBL).
P/E Ratio:
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) had the lowest P/E ratio at 9.60 times, followed by  Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at 11.35 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.82%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the lowest at 11.64%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.38%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.28%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 1.95% while
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest
ROE at 15.36%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.21%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.22%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 84.33%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 62.39%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.04%, and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 4.89%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.6% to 3.9%.
The table below provides a detailed overview of these financial indicators across the 20 commercial banks for Q4 FY 2081/82.

Headline: Commercial Banks Post Rs. 71.50 Arba Net Profit in Q4 FY 2081/82; Nabil Bank Leads Net Profit, Everest Bank Tops Distributable Profit Per Share
Full Content:
Nepal’s commercial banks have reported their net profits for the fourth quarter (Q4) of FY 2081-82, based on unaudited financial statements.
Net Profit:
Collectively, the 20 commercial banks posted a net profit of Rs. 71.50 Arba, reflecting a 43.39% year-on-year (YoY) growth compared to Rs. 49.86 Arba in the same period of FY 2080/81.
Nabil Bank Limited recorded the highest net profit, earning Rs. 7.13 Arba by the end of Ashad, a 15.01% increase from the previous year. Following Nabil, Nepal Investment Mega Bank posted Rs. 6.76 Arba, while Global IME Bank earned Rs. 6.20 Arba. NIC Asia Bank recorded the lowest net profit at Rs. 16 crores, experiencing the steepest YoY decline of 77.03% from Rs. 70 crores in FY 2080/81.
Kumari Bank reported the highest profit growth among all banks, with an increase of 45,820.14%. Other banks showing notable growth after revising previous year figures include Prabhu Bank and Nepal Bank.
However, four banks—Standard Chartered Bank, Nepal SBI Bank, Citizens Bank International, and NIC Asia Bank—recorded a decline in profit during the review period, with NIC Asia Bank’s net profit falling the most.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
In terms of distributable profit per share, Everest Bank Limited (EBL) led with Rs. 38.27 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.47. Despite being second in total net profit, Nepal Investment Mega Bank reported the lowest distributable profit per share at Rs. 1.44. Four banks recorded negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.

Headline: Citizen Investment Trust’s Provident & Pension Scheme Expands to NMLBBL and ULBSL Employees
Full Content:
Citizen Investment Trust’s provident and pension scheme has now included Nerude Mirmire Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (NMLBBL) and Upakar Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (ULBSL). The scheme allows organized institutions and their employees to participate on a contribution or non-contribution basis.
Started in 2055 BS, the program collects and invests contributions from employees, paying benefits upon retirement. Currently, 1,150 organizations with around 33,000 employees participate. Employees can access loans for housing, home renovation, and other personal, social, or cultural needs.

Headline: Citizens Bank Partners with E-Sport Nepal to Offer Exclusive Discounts and Boost Digital Banking
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited has signed an MoU with E-Sport Nepal to offer up to 10% discounts to its customers, including 5% off on EV charging and 5% on food. This partnership promotes digital transactions and enhances customer convenience.
Citizens Bank continues to lead in digital innovation, having introduced Nepal’s first virtual credit card and CRN application via its mobile app. With over 1.9 million customers and 200 branches nationwide, the bank aims to modernize banking and support financial inclusion through tech-driven services and strategic collaborations.

Headline: Citizens Bank Drives Financial Literacy Across Nepal with Extensive Programs
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) conducted financial literacy programs across all seven provinces in fiscal year 2081/82 through 148 branches, reaching around 100,000 individuals, including women, students, farmers, and migrant workers. The bank emphasized the importance of financial awareness, digital banking, and safe banking practices.
Alongside these efforts, CZBIL has introduced innovative services like Nepal’s first virtual credit card and mobile app-based share application. With over 200 branches and 19 lakh customers nationwide, the bank continues to provide modern banking services and contribute to community welfare.

Headline: Citizens Bank Mourns the Untimely Demise of Board Member Ila Sharma
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Ltd. mourns the untimely demise of board member Ila Sharma, who passed away at the age of 60 due to a heart attack on 2082/03/28 during treatment at Norvic Hospital.
Sharma, a former Election Commissioner and legal expert with over 35 years of experience, had been serving on the bank's committee for the past year. Her funeral was held at Aryaghat, attended by senior bank officials, staff, and shareholders. The bank expressed deep sorrow, calling her loss an irreparable one.

Headline: Citizens Capital Launches Nepal’s First Open-Ended Mutual Fund Scheme
Full Content:
Citizens Capital Limited, a leading merchant bank and subsidiary of Citizens Bank International, has launched Nepal’s first open-ended mutual fund scheme, the Citizens Sadabahar Scheme, under the Citizens Mutual Fund. Approved by the Securities Board of Nepal, the scheme opens for unit sales from Ashadh 13 to Ashadh 27, 2082 (June 27 – July 10, 2025) with a fund size of NPR 500 million.
Investors can subscribe via Mero Share or C-ASBA member banks, with investments ranging from NPR 1,000 to NPR 50 million. The scheme offers SIP options and expects an average annual return of 15.10%. Citizens Capital provides extensive financial services and nationwide access through Citizens Bank branches.

Headline: Citizens Bank Launches Online Loan Facility Against Fixed Deposits for Instant Access
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited has launched an online loan facility allowing customers to borrow up to 90% of their fixed deposits via its mobile app, with instant credit to their savings account and no paperwork required. This move enhances digital banking convenience.
The bank, which recently won the “Bank of the Year 2024” award, also introduced Nepal’s first virtual credit card in partnership with Fonepay and continues to expand its digital services, serving over 1.97 million customers through 200 branches and a robust digital network.

Headline: Citizens Capital Launches Open-Ended Mutual Fund ‘Sadabahar Yojana’ with 50 Million Units Offering
Full Content:
Citizens Capital Limited is launching a new open-ended mutual fund named ‘Citizens Sadabahar Yojana’, opening for public offering from Ashadh 13, 2082. The scheme aims to deliver long-term returns through a professionally managed diversified portfolio. A total of 50 million units will be issued at NPR 10 per unit, with 15% reserved for promoter Citizens Bank International Limited and the rest for public investors.
The fund allows redemption after 3 months and will not be listed on the stock exchange, but will maintain liquidity through authorized institutions. With prior success in mutual fund management and a flexible investment structure, Citizens Sadabahar Yojana is positioned to attract a wide range of retail and institutional investors in Nepal.

Headline: Citizens Bank Extends CSR Support to Akhanda Jyoti Trust and Promotes Inclusive Digital Banking
Full Content:
As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, Citizens Bank International Limited has extended support to the Akhanda Jyoti Baba Swami Shreeji Charitable Trust, an organization dedicated to helping the underprivileged through services in health, education, religious preservation, and women's empowerment. The Trust also offers free meals to pilgrims and manages facilities such as a rest house and a girls’ Gurukul.
The support was handed over in a special ceremony by the bank’s CEO, Mr. Ganesh Raj Pokharel, who expressed satisfaction in contributing to the Trust’s selfless efforts. The bank emphasized its ongoing commitment to social, economic, cultural, and educational development through various CSR programs.
In addition to its CSR efforts, Citizens Bank was recently recognized with the international title “Bank of the Year 2024.” The bank also launched Nepal’s first-ever virtual credit card, “Citizens Fonepay Credit Card,” in partnership with Fonepay. It continues to enhance its digital services with features such as share application, CRN services, and Cross Bank Teller QR for easier cash withdrawals.
The bank currently serves over 1.9 million customers across 61 districts through 200 branches, 168 ATMs, and digital platforms. Its new product, the Citizens Digital Fixed Deposit (CDFD), offers a convenient, paperless way to save, with flexible interest payouts and no charges in the first year, making it ideal for tech-savvy and busy individuals seeking higher returns.

Headline: Citizens Bank International Limited Promoted "Citizens Sadabahar Yojana" to Issue 4.25 Crore Units Mutual Fund Scheme to General Public From Ashadh 13
Full Content:
Citizens Capital Limited has published an offer letter to issue the
"Citizens Sadabahar Yojana"
open-ended mutual fund scheme. The issue will open from the 13th Ashadh to the 17th Ashadh, 2082. If not fully subscribed by the early closing date, the issue can be extended until Ashadh 27.
Out of 5 crore unit shares, 15%, i.e., 75 lakh units worth Rs. 7.50 crore, have been allocated to the scheme manager, Citizens Bank International Limited, and the remaining 4,25,00,000 units worth Rs 42.50 Crores will be issued to the general public and institutions.
"Citizens Sadabahar Yojana" is an open-ended fund. Applicants can apply for a minimum of 100 units to a maximum of 50,00,000 units.

Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) has signed an agreement with Teeka Resort, Lakeside Pokhara, to offer a 20% discount to its customers. The offer is available to Citizens Bank's cardholders, privilege cardholders, and mobile banking users, aiming to promote digital transactions over cash payments.
The bank believes this collaboration will encourage digital banking practices among its clients. Detailed information about the discounts can be found on the bank’s official website.
Citizens Bank, which recently won the prestigious "Bank of the Year 2024" award, has been actively expanding its digital services. It recently introduced Nepal’s first virtual credit card, Citizens FonePay Credit Card, and allows services like share applications and CRN numbers through its mobile banking app. It has also introduced cross-bank teller QR services, enabling customers of other banks to withdraw cash from Citizens Bank branches.
Currently, the bank serves over 1.9 million customers through 200 branches, 168 ATMs, 3 extension counters, and 74 branchless banking units across 61 districts in Nepal.

Headline: SEBON Approves Citizens Capital’s Mutual Fund Scheme "Citizens Sadabahar Yojana" To Issue 5 Crore Units
Full Content:
The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) has approved the
"Citizens Sadabahar Yojana"
worth Rs 50 crores on Ashadh 02, 2082.
This is an open-ended mutual fund scheme that will be floating 5 crore unit shares each at a par value of Rs 10 per share. The sponsor of the fund is Citizens Bank International Limited, while the fund manager is Citizens Capital Limited.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Baisakh; NABIL Tops the Charts Once More
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for till the tenth month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Baisakh.

Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 5.02 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the NIC Asia Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 47.87 Crores.
Development Banks:

Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 87.68 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank which posted Rs. 86.93 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 61.54 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Green Development Bank and Corporate Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 2.32 crores and Rs. 1.56 crores, respectively.
Furthermore, eight banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Salapa, Corporate Development Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Citizens Bank Leads Environmental Efforts with Tree Plantation and Digital Innovations
Full Content:
Citizens Bank has launched a large-scale tree plantation campaign in Dhangadhi under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, embracing the theme “Beat the Plastic” for World Environment Day 2025. Over 100 saplings were planted to promote environmental sustainability and combat climate change. The bank, known for its broad CSR efforts, also supports health camps, schools, and religious institutions.
Recently, it earned the “Bank of the Year 2024” award and introduced Nepal’s first virtual credit card in collaboration with FonePay. Citizens Bank has significantly enhanced its digital banking services, including features like stock applications, CRN requests, and cross-bank teller services. Serving over 1.89 million customers nationwide, the bank operates 200 branches and promotes eco-friendly savings through its digital fixed deposit product, Citizens Digital Fixed Deposit, which offers attractive returns and a paperless process.

Headline: Citizens Bank Enhances CSR and Digital Banking with New Shelter, Tree Plantation, and Virtual Credit Card Launch
Full Content:
As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Citizens Bank International Limited's Beni branch constructed a passenger waiting shelter in Jamunakhark, Ward No. 6 of Beni Municipality, for Rs. 50,000. Headline: Citizens Bank Launches Nepal's First Secure API Banking Platform ‘RAPID’
Full Content:
Citizens Bank International Limited, in collaboration with Gokyo Labs Pvt. Ltd., has launched RAPID (Real-time API Platform for Integration and Digitization), Nepal’s first secure API banking platform. Designed for corporate clients, RAPID allows seamless integration of a company's ERP system with its bank account, enabling real-time access to account balances and statements.
In the first phase, RAPID focuses on non-financial services, simplifying business operations by removing the need to log into online banking platforms. The upcoming second phase will enable secure digital transactions using global standards like ISO 20022, OAuth2, and Multi-Factor Authentication.
Features will include ERP-based payments, fund transfers, payroll processing, and online account opening. Security is enhanced through OAuth2-based digital consent, Time-based One-Time Passwords, and encrypted data using Public Key Infrastructure.
This API platform supports faster, more accurate, and data-driven decision-making for businesses, marking a major step in Nepal’s business banking digitization. RAPID aligns with Citizens Bank’s long-standing commitment to innovation, reflected in its recent “Bank of the Year 2024” award and expansive network of 200 branches across 61 districts. RAPID is expected to transform how Nepali businesses manage finances, offering greater control, speed, and security within their own operational systems.

Headline: Delving into Q3 2081/82: Performance Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks with Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the third quarter of FY 2081/82, offering a fresh look into their performance during the nine-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q3 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 5.05 Arba, marking an 8.21% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 4.54 Arba, though this represents a 38.61% increase from the previous year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 4.53 Arba.
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 2032.94% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 91.81%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.41 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 17.07 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 36.38 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 34.19 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 30.85 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 60.35 Kharba in customer deposits, with eight banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.18 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.02 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 4.01 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 77.26 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.31 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 12.32 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 12.05 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 35.07 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 5.17 Arba, with Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) next at Rs. 3.20 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 35.61, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at Rs. 28.86 and Nepal Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 25.26. The industry average EPS was Rs. 15.12, with eleven banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 1.40.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 28.42 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 16.19. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 332.66, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 264.85 and Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 260.74. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 134.43, with the industry average at Rs. 195.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) had the lowest P/E ratio at 9.94 times, followed by  Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at 11.92 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.44%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the lowest at 10.84%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.64%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.68%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 1.92% while
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest
ROE at 16.10%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.47%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.3%.
- CD Ratio:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) had the highest CD ratio at 85.90%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 64.37%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.20%, and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 5.02%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.8% to 4%.
The table below provides a detailed overview of these financial indicators across the 20 commercial banks for Q3 FY 2081/82.
**Note: All figures are reported in Arba except for net profit, which is presented in crores for clarity.

Headline: Performance Analysis of A-Class Banks in Q2 2081/82: Key Financial Metrics and Insights
Full Content:
The release of the second-quarter financial reports for FY 2081/82 by all 20 commercial banks sheds light on their financial performance, offering a detailed view of profitability, business volume, and key financial metrics. This analysis covers the second-quarter results, highlighting trends across net profit, capital adequacy, and other pivotal indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q2 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 3.24 Arba, marking a 1.29% increase over the same period last year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) followed with a net profit of Rs. 3.05 Arba, though this represents a 49.51% incline from the previous year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) took third with Rs. 2.83 Arba.
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 85.50% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 92.03%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.28 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 16.41 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 35.94 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 32.02 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 29.03 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 58.91 Kharba in customer deposits, with ten banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 4.8 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.47 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.07 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 3.91 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 78.17 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.27 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 8.30 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 7.9 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 24.67 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 3.27 Arba, with Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) next at Rs. 2.53 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 32.67, followed by Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 32.06 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 23.98. The industry average EPS was Rs. 14.72, with nine banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 2.03.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 20.99 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 13.25. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 329.84, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 261.96 and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 225.79. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 133.51, with the industry average at Rs. 190.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) had the lowest P/E ratio at 12.71 times, followed by Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at 12.81 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 16.94%, with Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) at 13.26%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.66%, while Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) reported the highest NPL at 6.96%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 2.16% and ROE at 16.10%. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with strong performances.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.69%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.38%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 86.76%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 63.20%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.52%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the lowest at 5.13%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.96% to 4%.

Headline: Commercial Banks Report 4.62% Decline in Net Profit for Q2 FY 2081/82; NABIL Leads, Prabhu Bank Sees Highest Growth
Full Content:
Nepal's commercial banks have reported a decrease in net profits for the second quarter of the current fiscal year, according to their unaudited financial statements. As of the end of Poush (mid-January), the 20 commercial banks collectively earned a net profit of Rs. 27.43 Arba, marking a 4.62% drop compared to the Rs. 28.76 Arba earned during the same period last year.
Out of the 20 banks, 9 recorded a decrease in net profits, contributing to the overall decline. However, 11 banks experienced growth in their earnings. Among these, Prabhu Bank stood out with the highest increase in net profit, reporting an impressive 85.49% rise. The bank's net profit surged from Rs. 72.03 Crores last year to Rs. 133.61 Crores this year. Similarly, Nepal Investment Mega Bank saw an increase of over 57.18%, while Global IME Bank's profit grew by 49.51%, and NMB Bank's profit rose by 45.61%.
On the other hand, NIC Asia Bank experienced the steepest drop in net profit, with a staggering 92.03% decrease. The bank’s profit plummeted from Rs. 1.90 Arba last year to just Rs. 15.17 Crores this year. Kumari Bank also saw a significant decline in net profit, falling by over 68.20%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank’s profit dropped by more than 62.14%.
Nabil Bank recorded the highest net profit for the quarter, amounting to Rs. 3.24 Arba, which marks a modest 1.29% increase from the same period last year. Global IME Bank also posted a strong performance, reporting a net profit exceeding Rs. 3 Arba.
During the second quarter, 11 commercial banks surpassed the Rs. 1 Arba mark in net profits. Among them, two banks reported more than Rs. 3 Arba in net profit, while three banks earned over Rs. 2 Arba. The remaining six banks each posted profits exceeding Rs. 1 Arba. Despite the overall decline in profits, the banking sector remains an important player in Nepal's financial landscape, with some institutions continuing to demonstrate significant growth.

Headline: Commercial Banks Reduce Base Interest Rates to 7.92% Amid Surplus Loanable Funds
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have reduced their average base interest rate to 7.92% for the period between mid-August and mid-September, driven by an excess of loanable funds. This marks a 0.25 percentage point decrease compared to the previous months, signaling a potential reduction in lending rates in the near future.
According to reports from the 20 commercial banks, Standard Chartered Bank has set the lowest base rate at 6.22%, followed by state-owned Rastriya Banijya Bank with a rate of 6.66%. On the higher end, NIC Asia Bank maintains the highest base rate at 9.22%, while Kumari Bank follows closely with 8.90%.
Over the past few months, banks have been gradually lowering their interest rates, with the average base rate consistently remaining in single digits since May 2024.
The lending rate of a bank is determined by adding a premium to its base rate, which typically ranges from 1.5% to 5%, depending on the nature of the loan and associated risks.
The reduction in base rates comes amid an economic slowdown, rising non-performing assets (NPAs), and challenges related to capital adequacy ratios. However, banks have shown improvement in key areas, including increased lending for auto loans and loans secured against shares as collateral. Records from Nepal Rastra Bank also reveal that banks have reduced a portion of their NPAs while strengthening their capital adequacy positions.
As lending rates are likely to follow the downward trend in base rates, businesses and individuals may benefit from more affordable loan opportunities in the coming months.

Return on Asset & Return on Equity
Return on Asset (ROA): ROA is a financial metric that measures a company's efficiency in generating profit from its assets. It indicates how effectively a company utilizes its assets to generate earnings. It is calculated by dividing the net income by the average total assets.
Return on Equity (ROE): ROE is a financial ratio that measures the profitability of a company in relation to its shareholders' equity. It shows how much profit a company generates with the money shareholders have invested. ROE is calculated by dividing net income by shareholders' equity.
In the fourth quarter, Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) emerged as the frontrunner among commercial banks, boasting an impressive Return on Asset (ROA) of 2.35% and Return on Equity (ROE) of 16.09%. Following closely behind, Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) exhibited a strong performance with an ROA of 1.40%, and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) with an ROE of 13.32%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, NMB Bank Limited (NMB) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.31%, whereas Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) has the lowest cost of funds at 3.84%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Likewise, Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 86.20%, whereas Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) has the lowest CD ratio of 60.82%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which Commercial banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) reports the highest base rate of 9.19%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest base rate of 6.60%.
Similarly, the net interest rate spread is the difference between the interest rate a bank pays to depositors and the interest rate it receives from loans to consumers. Here, the commercial banks have net interest rate spread hovering around 3.95%- 4%
